chunks.doc_title: University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements
chunks.section: Degree Credit Structure and Course Registration
chunks.text:
[University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements > Degree Credit Structure and Course Registration]
Undergraduate engineering degree programs require the successful completion of a minimum of 160 academic credits distributed across Basic Sciences, Engineering Core, Professional Electives, Open Electives, and Capstone Projects. Course registration occurs during the first three days of each semester through the Student Information System. Late registration is permitted up to five days with an approved penalty fee.

chunks.doc_title: University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements
chunks.text:
[University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements > Course Prerequisite Policy]
Students cannot register for an advanced course without successfully clearing its listed prerequisite subjects with a passing grade. Any conditional prerequisite waiver requires written recommendation from the course instructor and approval by the Departmental Academic Committee prior to course registration.

chunks.doc_title: University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements
chunks.text:
[University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements > Academic Probation and CGPA Retention]
A student must maintain a minimum CGPA of 5.0 at the end of each academic year to remain in good academic standing. If a student's CGPA falls below 5.0, they will be placed on Academic Probation for one semester. Students on probation have their maximum registered credits capped at 18 credits and must attend mandatory remedial advisory sessions.

chunks.doc_title: University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements
chunks.text:
[University Academic Policies and Degree Requirements > Honors and Minor Degrees]
Students with a consistent CGPA of 8.0 or higher, with no historical course backlogs, may opt for an Honors degree in their primary discipline or a Minor degree in a secondary engineering or computing specialization by completing an additional 18–20 specialized credits between semesters 4 and 8.

[University Attendance Policy > Minimum Attendance Requirement]
All registered undergraduate and postgraduate students must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in each enrolled theory and laboratory course during a semester to be eligible for end-semester examinations. Attendance is calculated from the official semester commencement date until the last instructional day announced in the academic calendar.

[University Attendance Policy > Condonation of Attendance Shortage]
Students with attendance between 65% and 74.9% may apply to the Dean of Academic Affairs for attendance condonation on genuine medical or compassionate grounds. The application must include an official medical certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner within seven working days of returning to campus, along with a nominal condonation fee. Condonation is granted at the sole discretion of the Academic Review Board.

[University Attendance Policy > Debarment Due to Attendance Shortage]
Students with aggregate course attendance below 65% under any circumstances are considered debarred from appearing in the end-semester examination for that specific course. Debarred students receive an 'F-Attendance' (FA) grade and are required to re-register for the course in a subsequent semester or summer term when the course is offered.

[University Attendance Policy > Attendance Monitoring and Discrepancies]
Course instructors update daily attendance in the University Academic ERP portal within 48 hours of conducting each class. Students are responsible for reviewing their attendance record weekly. Any discrepancy must be reported in writing to the respective course coordinator within five business days of attendance posting.

chunks.doc_title: University Campus Facilities and Resource Access
chunks.section: Central Library and Digital Resource Timings
chunks.text:
[University Campus Facilities and Resource Access > Central Library and Digital Resource Timings]
The Central University Library remains open Monday through Saturday from 08:00 AM to 10:00 PM, and on Sundays and recognized holidays from 10:00 AM to 06:00 PM. During final examination weeks, reading halls operate on a 24-hour schedule. Registered students may borrow up to four books simultaneously for a borrowing period of 14 calendar days using their barcode-enabled Student ID Card.

chunks.doc_title: University Campus Facilities and Resource Access
chunks.text:
[University Campus Facilities and Resource Access > High-Performance Computing and Cloud Labs]
The Computing Center provides access to high-performance GPU clusters, cloud development sandboxes, and virtualized container environments for authorized coursework and faculty-mentored research. Access is granted through university institutional Single Sign-On (SSO). Accounts inactive for 90 days are automatically decommissioned.

chunks.doc_title: University Campus Facilities and Resource Access
chunks.text:
[University Campus Facilities and Resource Access > Maker Space and Hardware Prototyping]
The Advanced Innovation Maker Space offers 3D printers, laser cutters, CNC milling units, and electronics test benches. All students must complete mandatory Workshop Safety Orientation prior to operating heavy machinery. Consumables such as PLA filament and soldering supplies are requisitioned through the department portal.

chunks.doc_title: University Campus Facilities and Resource Access
chunks.text:
[University Campus Facilities and Resource Access > Sports Complex and Fitness Facilities]
The indoor sports arena encompasses badminton courts, table tennis stations, squash courts, and a supervised gymnasium. Facility timings are 06:00 AM to 09:00 AM in the morning and 04:30 PM to 08:30 PM in the evening. Clean non-marking sports shoes and valid sports registration tags are mandatory for arena entry.

chunks.section: Examination Hall Entry and Admit Card
chunks.text:
[University Examination Rules and Regulations > Examination Hall Entry and Admit Card]
Students must arrive at the examination hall at least 15 minutes before the scheduled commencement of the examination. No candidate will be admitted after 30 minutes from the start time. Every student must present a valid physical University Identity Card and official Examination Admit Card signed by the Controller of Examinations. Digital ID cards on mobile devices are not permitted.

[University Examination Rules and Regulations > Prohibited Items and Electronics]
Mobile phones, smartwatches, programmable calculators, Bluetooth earphones, storage media, and unauthorized written materials are strictly prohibited inside the examination venue. Possession of any electronic communication device, whether powered on or off, is categorized as a Category-1 examination violation and results in immediate confiscation and disciplinary investigation.

[University Examination Rules and Regulations > Grading System and Passing Standards]
The university operates on a 10-point Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) system. Course grades range from 'O' (Outstanding - 10 points) down to 'P' (Pass - 4 points) and 'F' (Fail - 0 points). To successfully earn course credits, a student must secure at least 40% marks in the end-semester examination and an aggregate of 45% when combined with continuous internal evaluations.

[University Examination Rules and Regulations > Supplementary Examinations and Revaluation]
Students who receive an 'F' grade in a theoretical course may appear for a Supplementary Examination conducted before the start of the following academic year. Students dissatisfied with their evaluation may submit a formal request for answer script revaluation or transparency photocopy within ten working days of result declaration through the Controller of Examinations portal.

[Student Leave Regulations and Protocols > Casual Leave and Absence Notification]
Students are eligible for up to six days of approved casual leave per academic semester for personal, domestic, or emergent circumstances. A leave application must be submitted via the student portal at least 24 hours prior to the intended leave date, accompanied by parental or guardian authorization.

chunks.section: Medical Leave and Health Center Certification
chunks.text:
[Student Leave Regulations and Protocols > Medical Leave and Health Center Certification]
In the event of severe illness or hospitalization, medical leave up to a maximum of 15 calendar days per semester may be recognized. The student or guardian must notify the Department Head within 48 hours of illness onset. Upon return, the student must report to the University Health Center for fitness verification with original hospital discharge summaries and medical prescriptions.

chunks.section: Duty Leave for Competitions and Conferences
chunks.text:
[Student Leave Regulations and Protocols > Duty Leave for Competitions and Conferences]
Students representing the university in state or national sports events, technical hackathons, academic conferences, or cultural symposiums are granted On-Duty (OD) attendance credit. The faculty coordinator of the respective club or sports director must endorse and submit the OD approval form to the Academic Registrar prior to the event.

[Student Leave Regulations and Protocols > Long-Term Semester Withdrawal]
A student who experiences prolonged medical incapacitation requiring absence of more than four continuous weeks may petition the Academic Council for a formal Semester Withdrawal without academic penalty. Courses for that semester will be marked as 'Withdrawn' (W) and tuition fee adjustment is governed by university refund bylaws.
